Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — FinBridge's procurement team asked for a more detailed breakdown of exactly where customer request and artifact data can be processed, stored, or routed (regions and any subprocessor hops). They're specifically asking: 

- A simple matrix that maps data types (request payload, cached KV, logs, metrics, embeddings) to processing locations and subprocessors.
- Whether any step (including backups, analytics, or monitoring) leaves the EU when we enable EU residency.
- What guarantees or contractual controls you offer to pin processing to an EU region (if available) and the expected residual transfer paths for third-party services.

I attached our MRAP questionnaire and highlighted the residency bit (see attachment). Can you send an internal diagram or matrix we can share with Legal and Security? Ideally we'd like it by EOD Monday so we can include it in our vendor review for the board.

Thanks — appreciate it.

Hi Kristen — attaching a technical matrix and an annotated subprocessor summary. High level answers below, and more detail in the attachments.

TL;DR:
- We support EU-only processing for request/response payloads and KV/cache (pin to eu-west-1 or eu-central-1) when a customer chooses the EU residency option.
- Some peripheral telemetry (aggregated metrics, usage analytics) may be processed in the US by default for platform analytics, but we offer a toggle to route customer telemetry to EU-only analytics for enterprise plans; that requires the residency flag + addendum.
- Backups and long-term logs: primary backups for EU-resident workloads remain in the EU for the retention window; disaster-recovery (DR) replicas may be in a paired region (EU or UK) depending on customer choice. We do not replicate EU production data into the US unless explicitly requested in writing.
- Subprocessors: listed in the PDF with processing role and data flow arrows (storage, monitoring, analytics). Third-party CDN endpoints only carry ephemeral request traffic and do not persist customer data.

Important notes:
- Cross-border transfers: if EU residency is selected, token-level inference requests and model execution remain in-region. However, model updates, telemetry aggregation, and certain third-party managed services may have supporting control-plane operations that touch other regions — these are described in the subprocessor doc and covered by contractual controls and SCCs where applicable.
- Contracting: Laura, can you confirm the standard addendum language we offer for EU pinning and whether a Data Processing Addendum + SCCs are sufficient or whether FinBridge needs an amendment?

Attachments included:
- regional-processing-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 42 KB) — mapping of data category -> primary processing region -> subprocessors -> transfer hops.
- redwood-subprocessors-annotated.pdf (PDF, 128 KB) — vendor list, roles, and transfer notes.

If anything in the matrix looks off or you want a regional diagram with arrows broken down by subprocessor, I can produce a one-page diagram for Legal.

— Dev

Hi Kristen — quick answers and next steps. Laura is looping in on the DPA/SCCs and will propose precise contract language; she flagged the same items below.

Short answers now:
- DR replicas: under standard enterprise EU residency, DR replicas are placed in a geographically adjacent EU region (e.g., eu-west-1 <-> eu-central-1). We do not replicate EU production or backups to US regions unless a customer has signed a separate DR replication addendum or requests it explicitly in writing. Any such replication is documented, time-boxed and subject to controls and redaction options; we can provide a paper trail for audits.
- Telemetry: EU-only telemetry is available for Dedicated and Private customers. For Hosted customers it is available as an enterprise feature behind an addendum; lead time is usually 2-4 weeks to update pipelines and validate retention controls.
- Contracting: Laura will share the DPA + SCC pack and we can include a clause committing to "no routine cross-border transfer" for production data for EU-resident customers unless explicitly agreed in writing.

Next actions:
1) Laura will send the recommended DPA language and the standard SCCs by Monday morning.
2) Dev will produce a one-page diagram showing DR pairing and telemetry flows for the board packet.
3) Marissa to schedule a 30-min call between FinBridge Legal, Dev and Laura next week to close open items.
